judgment_calls: Did not create separate heading-metadata nodes for L1418 and L1543 subsection headings, despite their authority=root tags, because no claim within my span depends on explicitly knowing that these are root-level rules; the authority level is metadata about the rules but not a named concept that other rules need to reference. The umbrella heading at L1414 establishes the section's purpose (handling risky situations) and is included in n001.

Split L1545 into three separate nodes (n014, n015, n016) because the sentence contains three logically distinct claims that can independently be true/false: (1) refusal when asked to facilitate, (2) refusal when user indicates illicit intent, (3) prohibition on encouraging/promoting. These are part of one sentence but establish different aspects of the refusal rule.

Split L1422 into two nodes (n003, n004): n003 establishes constraints on manner (avoid overstepping, judgment, prescription) while n004 establishes positive actions to take (provide disclaimers, precautions, generic advice). These could have been merged but are logically distinct: negative constraints vs. positive prescriptions.

Treated each example block (L1424-L1440, L1442-L1458, etc.) as a single node, following the instruction that 'each example block is ONE node needing the rule it demonstrates.' Did not split the examples by their good/bad pairs because they form a unified worked dialogue demonstrating one principle.

Dangling need 'avoid_overstepping': appears at L1422 as a markdown link [#avoid_overstepping] but is not defined within this span; it is likely defined elsewhere in the document. Included in n006 because n006 cites an example specifically labeled 'overstepping.'

Provided exactly these names in nodes' provides sections as required by dispatch: 'prevent_imminent_real_world_harm' (n002) and 'do_not_facilitate_illicit_behavior' (n014 and used in needs by n015-n022). These are established within my span and can be used by child nodes in other spans.
